tex_content.html:
For a three-dimensional flow satisfying Proposition 3.2, its splitting limit is the product of a shrinking family of compact round surfaces with a line. This applies in particular to noncompact asymptotic solitons of three-dimensional $\kappa $-solutions.
Proof

\sketch ↗ prop:splitting-at-infinity ↗ cor:two-dimensional-gradient-shrinking-soliton The surface factor inherits nonflat nonnegative bounded curvature, $\partial _tR\geq 0$, and $\kappa '$-non-collapsing. The two-dimensional classification therefore makes it compact and round.

□

Corollary
[Asymptotic soliton of a 3D $\kappa $-solution has bounded curvature]

copy_context.title: 3Dinfty
copy_context.description:
\label{3Dinfty}

For a three-dimensional flow satisfying
Proposition~\ref{prop:splitting-at-infinity}, its splitting limit is
the product of a shrinking family of compact round surfaces with a
line. This applies in particular to noncompact asymptotic solitons
of three-dimensional $\kappa$-solutions.
\end{corollary}
